claims.exact_statement: For every Boolean core g on a uniform data cube and all mutually disjoint fresh selector blocks W_j of positive sizes k_j, arbitrary translation vectors v_j and point indicators A_j, set F(w,y)=g(y+sum_j v_j A_j(w_j)). With rho_j=Pr[g(y)!=g(y+v_j)] and E_k=H(1-2*1_point) on k bits, H(F)=H(g)+sum_j rho_j E_kj, I_data(F)=I(g), I_W(F)=sum_j rho_j 2 k_j 2^(-k_j), M_W=0 and B_W=sum_j rho_j E_kj<=4 I_W(F). Constant 4 is optimal as I_W/|W| tends to zero. A certified core FEI constant C transfers to max(C,4), including arbitrary finite nesting with fresh selector modules. Complete-module block trees have the same payment and retain terminal core entropy. The constant 4 cannot be assigned to every singleton query, as the three-bit point module on a dictator shows.
hypotheses: Uniform independent physical coordinates; entropy in bits
Selector module blocks pairwise disjoint and fresh from current data
g Boolean; vectors may coincide or be linearly dependent
Translation activation in each module is exactly one point
An FEI bound on the arbitrary terminal core is an additional hypothesis only for full-entropy closure
